name: Amcor plc
moat_justification: Largest consumer-packaging supplier globally with real qualification switching costs in food/health packaging and a dense plant network, but largely commoditized products sold to powerful FMCG customers, contractual pass-through rather than structural pricing power, low returns on capital through the cycle, and high post-Berry leverage — a moderate/narrow moat.
fragility_flags: BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 32.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.1x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Narrow-moat global packaging leader (moat 5/10) mid-Berry-integration — at $43.74 it prices in the synergy bull case and does not clear 15% on the weighted case (10.4% weighted IRR, IV@15% $26.84); it clears 15% only at or below $26.84.
moat_for: Global scale: largest consumer packaging supplier, 400+ locations in 40+ countries
Customer qualification switching costs in food and healthcare packaging
Dense plant network located close to FMCG customers
Materials-science and sustainability innovation; Berry adds dispensing and closures
$650M Berry synergy program, $285M delivered in FY2026
moat_against: Largely commoditized products; customers are powerful global FMCG groups
Resin/raw-material costs passed through — pricing power is contractual, not structural
Low returns on capital through the cycle for a capital-intensive plant base
High leverage: reported net debt $12.9B at ~3.5x (FY2026 earnings reporting)
Organic volumes negative in FY2026 (-2%); regulatory pressure on plastics packaging
